must-fix.issue: Restored execution state has no explicit authority reset. Consent revalidation is specified, but restored approvals, queued/in-flight jobs, submission intents and unsettled reservations are not assigned a nonexecuting restore state.
must-fix.risk: A database backup is a past observation of external effects. An effect may have completed after that snapshot. Existing supervisor startup requeues interrupted local attempts; carrying that behavior into restored workflow/provider jobs could replay an approved effect, reuse stale authority or release/reuse an unsettled reservation. The plan promises duplicate-free resume without defining this restore boundary.
must-fix.repair: Specify a new workspace execution identity on restore; invalidate or explicitly revalidate pending human approvals and grants; suspend queued jobs and quarantine/reconcile interrupted attempts and external intents before supervisor admission. Preserve external request IDs and unsettled reservations for account-scoped reconciliation, and forbid automatic provider resubmission or automatic reservation release. Require a new approved run for new effects. Propagate the rule into YU-013/014/061/080, the task registry and acceptance matrix.
must-fix.requiredEvidence: Future deterministic stand-in fixtures restore snapshots captured before submit, after intent/before acknowledgement, after effect/before receipt, and after approval; opening the restored workspace starts no effects, preserves uncertain amounts and request identities, and cannot consume the prior approval. This review did not execute these fixtures.

worth-considering.issue: The 8 MiB canvas target lacks a document transport budget decision; the existing general request cap is 2 MiB.
worth-considering.risk: An implementation may globally raise ingress limits to accommodate creative documents, weakening unrelated command/MCP admission bounds, or may claim 8 MiB persistence while all transports reject it.
worth-considering.repair: Before YU-010 implementation, choose a bounded staged document upload/handle flow or a separately versioned per-command cap including UTF-8/envelope expansion, concurrency and aggregate memory limits. Keep the existing snapshot cap and unrelated request limits. Add exact-boundary and multibyte parity cases across enabled transports.
worth-considering.evidence: core/command/policy.ts:16-17 enforces 2 MiB request/snapshot maxima; YU-010 asks to measure an 8 MiB bounded canvas while retaining the snapshot cap.

worth-considering.issue: Stand-in isolation negatives should explicitly require positive controls in the same receipt.
worth-considering.risk: A broken stand-in, unreadable sentinel or unreachable test endpoint can make denied file/network attempts appear to prove isolation even when the operation was never exercised.
worth-considering.repair: Require the stand-in to prove it can read its granted input, write its private staging output and execute the same attempted operation in an approved unrestricted control process. Use deterministic test-owned endpoints/sentinels and record attempted operations plus denial evidence. Keep real GPU/driver qualification separate.
worth-considering.evidence: E1/YU-041 already require actual file/network/process negatives and fail-closed unsupported profiles; explicit controls would make the resulting evidence harder to misinterpret.
